dimensions.question: How does Moxy NYC Times Square present hotel stays, dining, social space, coworking, events and local participation before a user chooses a relationship with the property?
dimensions.scopeChange: Tests whether a lifestyle hotel presents one lodging funnel or multiple participation pathways under the same institutional identity.

observations.text: The property presents accommodation alongside multiple dining, rooftop, event and social-space experiences rather than as a room-only hotel.
Bar Moxy is explicitly described as part bar, part lounge and part coworking space.
The event proposition addresses both hotel-related groups and local or external users.

unanswered: How users distinguish hotel-guest benefits from generally public venue access before booking.
Whether users understand which services are hotel-operated, partner-operated or independent.
Which discovery pathways produce hotel bookings versus dining, event or local visitation.
dimensions.reason: Public operator evidence establishes multiple participation pathways but not representative user comprehension or conversion behavior.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Test the room, dining, rooftop and event discovery journeys separately and capture boundary language shown before commitment.

dimensions.question: Which Moxy experiences use separate booking, reservation or inquiry mechanisms, and does one relationship guarantee access or capacity in another?
dimensions.scopeChange: Tests parallel commitment systems across hotel rooms, restaurants, rooftop access, events and group business.

observations.text: Hotel rooms, restaurant tables, rooftop tables and special events use distinct commitment pathways.
Magic Hour accepts reservations and walk-ins, while hotel-guest priority remains subject to capacity, private events and doorman discretion.
Magic Hour event and bottle-service inquiries do not themselves guarantee a reservation.

unanswered: How competing hotel-guest, public, table-service and event demand is prioritized internally.
Whether hotel packages ever create guaranteed dining or rooftop inventory.
How failed or oversubscribed reservation attempts are recovered.
dimensions.reason: Separate reservation systems and conditional access are publicly visible, but internal inventory and prioritization rules are not.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Test live hotel, restaurant and event commitment flows, including unavailable dates and capacity-conflict conditions.

dimensions.question: What access rules, expectations, benefits and responsibility boundaries are established before a hotel guest or event customer physically arrives?
dimensions.scopeChange: Adds pre-arrival entitlement and routing questions across hotel, dining, rooftop and event relationships.

observations.text: Hotel guest information establishes venue-access conditions and key-card-linked benefits before or during the stay.
Event customers enter a separate inquiry process with event-specific contact and availability handling.
Published hotel information specifies check-in, checkout and luggage handling conditions.

unanswered: Which guest instructions are delivered automatically after booking.
Whether restaurant or event bookings are recognized in the hotel guest profile.
How responsibility is explained when a guest uses partner-operated venues.
dimensions.reason: Public pages establish several pre-arrival rules but do not expose the complete digital communication or identity-linking sequence.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Inspect confirmation flows, terms, pre-arrival communications and any cross-system identity or reservation linking visible to a customer.

dimensions.question: How are hotel guests, visitors, diners, rooftop customers and event attendees distinguished or routed when they reach the property?
dimensions.scopeChange: Tests whether physical arrival at one address creates uniform access or role-specific routing.

observations.text: Bar Moxy performs a dual social and hotel-arrival role, including hotel check-in.
Hotel guests use a room key to demonstrate priority status for Magic Hour, but entry remains conditional.
Magic Hour has a dedicated entry and elevator path distinct from ordinary hotel circulation.

unanswered: How staff distinguish overlapping user roles during peak periods.
What happens when hotel guests expect access that cannot be provided.
How event attendees and general public visitors are routed relative to hotel guests.
dimensions.reason: Public evidence establishes differentiated arrival and access mechanisms, but not representative frontline routing or exception handling.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Observe or document public arrival instructions for hotel, rooftop, dining and event users and capture exception scenarios.

dimensions.question: What does the hotel-room relationship actually entitle a guest to, and which co-located experiences remain separate or conditional?
dimensions.scopeChange: Separates the room product from public, social, dining, visitor and partner-operated services within the property.

observations.text: The hotel stay provides a room relationship while many prominent social and dining experiences remain separately governed.
Hotel guests receive some role-specific benefits, including Magic Hour priority and complimentary drip coffee during stated hours.
Visitors of hotel guests must be registered with the hotel rather than receiving automatic access through the guest relationship.

unanswered: Which property spaces require a room key beyond guest-room circulation.
How guest status is recognized across partner-operated services.
Which guest benefits are contractual entitlements versus discretionary privileges.
dimensions.reason: Public material demonstrates differentiated benefits and access rules but not the complete entitlement architecture.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Map every publicly documented guest benefit, access restriction and partner-service condition against the hotel room relationship.

dimensions.question: How are Moxy's food-and-beverage venues related to the hotel, and where do reservation, entitlement, capacity and operator responsibility remain separate?
dimensions.scopeChange: Tests dining as a set of distinct commercial and operational relationships rather than a single hotel amenity.

observations.text: Bar Moxy, Legasea, Magic Hour and CafÃ© d'Avignon use different service and reservation conditions.
CafÃ© d'Avignon is physically on-site but Marriott explicitly describes it as unaffiliated with Moxy Times Square.
Restaurant, rooftop and event contacts route through TAO Group addresses rather than the hotel's general contact channel.

unanswered: Exact contractual responsibility across Moxy, TAO Group and other on-site operators.
How hotel complaints involving partner-operated dining are resolved.
Whether guest-spend data crosses hotel and restaurant systems.
dimensions.reason: Public evidence strongly establishes distinct venue relationships and responsibility signals but not internal contracts or recovery processes.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Inspect terms, booking interfaces and responsibility language for each on-site food-and-beverage operator.

dimensions.question: Which Moxy relationships end at checkout and which can continue through luggage handling, loyalty, dining, events or future engagement?
dimensions.scopeChange: Tests whether physical hotel departure closes the wider institutional relationship.

observations.text: The hotel publishes a defined checkout time while separately supporting luggage storage.
Luggage storage has its own stated responsibility limitation.
The public evidence reviewed does not establish that dining, event or wider brand relationships terminate when the room stay ends.

unanswered: How post-stay marketing, loyalty and return-visit relationships are handled.
Whether restaurant or event relationships remain linked to the former hotel guest.
How post-checkout service recovery is routed between hotel and partner operators.
dimensions.reason: Checkout and luggage rules are visible, but post-stay relationship continuity is not sufficiently documented.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Inspect Marriott Bonvoy, post-stay communication and venue-specific retention pathways without assuming cross-system continuity.

dimensions.question: How does Moxy use shared social space, programming and event activity to serve both hotel guests and non-guests?
dimensions.scopeChange: Treats atmosphere as an operating layer that may deliberately mix user roles within shared physical space.

observations.text: Bar Moxy is positioned as a combined work, play and social environment rather than a conventional hotel lobby.
The property explicitly markets Bar Moxy to both guests and locals.
Rooftop and social spaces support both ordinary hospitality use and private event conversion.

unanswered: How public and hotel-guest use compete during high-demand periods.
Whether event conversion materially displaces ordinary guest use.
How atmosphere changes across daytime coworking, dining, nightlife and private-event modes.
dimensions.reason: The intended mixed-role atmosphere is well documented, but actual user mix, displacement and operational effects are not.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Compare published operating modes, event schedules and access conditions across different times and uses.

dimensions.question: What relationships and spaces does Moxy emphasize visually, and do those images clarify or blur the distinction between lodging and public social hospitality?
dimensions.scopeChange: Tests visual communication as evidence of how the institution wants users to understand hotel, dining, social and event functions.

observations.text: Official imagery prominently features Bar Moxy, Magic Hour, dining and event environments alongside hotel accommodation.
The visual emphasis presents social and shared spaces as central components of the property identity rather than peripheral amenities.

unanswered: Whether prospective guests accurately infer access conditions from the imagery.
Whether photography distinguishes public, guest-priority and privately reservable spaces.
How room imagery compares quantitatively with social and event imagery across discovery channels.
dimensions.reason: Official visual emphasis is observable, but audience interpretation and quantitative image balance have not been tested.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Perform a bounded gallery review and record which user roles, spaces and access states are represented or omitted.

dimensions.question: What institutional story connects rooms, social space, dining, work and events, and where does the unified brand narrative mask distinct access or responsibility structures?
dimensions.scopeChange: Tests whether one hospitality story overlays several operationally distinct relationships.

observations.text: Moxy presents the property as an unconventional hotel built around social interaction, work, play, dining and events.
The unified property story includes services with materially different booking and operating relationships.
The public-facing brand can appear institutionally unified even where contact routing or affiliation indicates separate responsibility.

unanswered: How clearly customers understand the distinction between Moxy, Marriott, TAO Group and unaffiliated on-site operators.
Whether the unified brand story creates service expectations that exceed actual entitlement.
How responsibility is communicated when a cross-service experience fails.
dimensions.reason: The unified brand narrative and several responsibility boundaries are visible, but customer interpretation and operational consequences remain untested.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Compare brand language, venue terms, contact routing and customer-facing responsibility statements across services.
